title: Localization of a fibred ringed site at a scheme test object
statement:
Work in the universes and small-site convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $p:\mathcal C\to\mathit{Sch}/S$ a category fibred in groupoids [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. For $\tau\in\{\mathrm{et},\mathrm{fppf}\}$ give $\mathcal C$ the topology whose coverings lie over jointly surjective scheme coverings for $\tau$, and the structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}(z)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ for $z$ over $T$ [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]; in the etale case the scheme maps are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and in the fppf case use [def-pc-fppf-site]. Let $x\in\mathcal C$ lie over $U$. The functor $p_x:\mathcal C/x\to\mathit{Sch}/U$ sends an arrow $z\to x$ to its underlying scheme map $T\to U$. With the localized topology and restricted ring sheaf [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], this is an equivalence of ringed sites
$$ (\mathcal C_\tau/x,\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}|_x)\simeq((\mathit{Sch}/U)_\tau,\mathcal O). $$
The equivalence sends the terminal object $\mathrm{id}_x$ to $\mathrm{id}_U$ and identifies the value of both ring sheaves on an object over $T$ with $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. For every module sheaf $M$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the localized module $M|_x$ corresponds to the module $x^{-1}M$ on $(\mathit{Sch}/U)_\tau$ obtained by evaluating $M$ on cartesian lifts of schemes over $U$, with the original restriction maps. These identifications are compatible with further restriction along arrows $x'\to x$. No algebraicity, representability, quasi-coherence or flatness hypothesis on $\mathcal C$ or $M$ is required.

proof.text: For arrows $a:z\to x$ and $b:w\to x$, a morphism $a\to b$ in the slice is a map $c:z\to w$ with $bc=a$. For each scheme map $v:p(z)\to p(w)$ satisfying $p(b)v=p(a)$, the unique-factorization clause of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] gives exactly one such $c$ over $v$. Thus $p_x$ gives a bijection on every Hom set. In particular, two lifts of the same $T\to U$ have unique maps in both directions over $\mathrm{id}_T$; their composites are identities by the same uniqueness. This proves full faithfulness and the unique compatible isomorphism between any two choices of lift.

source.place: Tag 0CN0, lemma-localizing, proof; Categories Tag 003T, definition-fibred-groupoids

proof.text: For every $u:T\to U$, lift $u$ to $q_u:u^*x\to x$ by [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Choose these lifts in the small universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with $q_{\mathrm{id}_U}=\mathrm{id}_x$. Send a map $v:(T,u)\to(T',u')$ to the unique map $c_v:u^*x\to(u')^*x$ over $v$ satisfying $q_{u'}c_v=q_u$. The uniqueness in step 1 gives $c_{\mathrm{id}}=\mathrm{id}$ and $c_{v'v}=c_{v'}c_v$, so this is a functor $Q_x$. We have $p_xQ_x=\mathrm{id}$; the unique slice isomorphisms of step 1 give $Q_xp_x\cong\mathrm{id}$, natural because the two maps in each naturality square have the same base map and composite to $x$. Hence $p_x$ is an equivalence, and it sends $\mathrm{id}_x$ to $\mathrm{id}_U$.

By [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], a family in $\mathcal C/x$ covers precisely when its underlying family in $\mathcal C$ covers. By the topology in the hypothesis this means precisely that its image under $p_x$ is a jointly surjective $\tau$-family of schemes over $U$. Conversely $Q_x$ lifts any such family and keeps exactly its underlying scheme maps, so the lifted family covers. The same argument applies with any target $a:z\to x$, not just $\mathrm{id}_x$. Thus both quasi-inverse functors preserve coverings, which is the asserted equivalence of sites. No stack descent or algebraicity is used.

source.place: Tag 0CN0, lemma-localizing, proof (inherited topology); stacks-sheaves.tex Tag 06W0, lemma-localizing

proof.text: At $a:z\to x$ over $T\to U$, the restricted ring sheaf has value $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}(z)=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] and [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra]. This is exactly the value of $\mathcal O$ on $T/U$. An arrow over $v:T\to T'$ acts on both rings by the same regular-function pullback $v^*$. The identity on these rings therefore gives an isomorphism of ring sheaves under $p_x$, with inverse also the identity. Together with step 3 this is the equivalence of ringed sites in the statement.

Put $N=M|_x$. By [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] its value at $a:z\to x$ is $M(z)$. Precomposing $N$ with $Q_x$ gives the presheaf $G(T\xrightarrow{u}U)=M(u^*x)$, with restriction $M(c_v)$ along $v$. By [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] this is a module over $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ and the maps $M(c_v)$ are semilinear over $v^*$, as required. The ring identification of step 4 changes no action or restriction. This is exactly the meaning of $x^{-1}M$ in definition-pullback following Tag 06W0: the restriction to $\mathcal C/x$ viewed through its equivalence with schemes over $U$.

source.place: Tag 06W0 and definition-pullback; paragraph after Tag 06W9

proof.text: The presheaf $G$ in step 5 is a sheaf: for a covering in $\mathit{Sch}/U$, step 3 gives the corresponding covering under $Q_x$. Its overlap objects correspond too, since a map to a fibre product is a pair of maps with equal composites, and the Hom bijections of step 1 identify exactly these pairs in the two categories. The sheaf equalizer diagram in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] for $G$ is therefore the sheaf equalizer diagram for $N$ on that lifted covering. Precomposition with $p_x$ works in the reverse direction by the identical argument. The isomorphisms of step 2, evaluated by these sheaves, are inverse natural module isomorphisms; module morphisms are transported componentwise. Consequently the ringed-site equivalence indeed gives the stated correspondence of module sheaves, independently up to canonical isomorphism of the lift choices.

source.place: Definition-pullback following Tag 06W0; paragraph after Tag 06W9 (expanded sheaf check)

proof.text: Let $a:x'\to x$ lie over $f:U'\to U$. The functors sending $(z\xrightarrow{b}x')$ to $(z\xrightarrow{ab}x)$ and $(T\xrightarrow{u}U')$ to $(T\xrightarrow{fu}U)$ form a strictly commuting square with $p_{x'}$ and $p_x$. On rings both routes give $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ and on modules both give $M(z)$ with the original maps, by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. More explicitly, if $q'_u:u^*x'\to x'$ and $q_{fu}:(fu)^*x\to x$ are independently chosen lifts, step 1 gives a unique isomorphism $h:u^*x'\to(fu)^*x$ over $\mathrm{id}_T$ with $q_{fu}h=aq'_u$. The component $M(h)$ identifies $M((fu)^*x)$ with $M(u^*x')$. Naturality and the identity/composition compatibilities hold because both candidate arrows over each base map have equal composite to $x$, so are equal by the unique-factorization clause of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. This proves the claimed compatibility with further restriction, without imposing a cartesian condition on $M$.
